text: The renowned Confucian hero Mr. Zeng Wen wrote this work, distilling the Four Books, the Five Classics, and the Thirteen Classics. It holds that a gentleman is watchful even in solitude, that the heart shows itself in conduct and knowledge takes form in ritual, that he is neither arrogant nor servile, and that his words and deeds are one. Let the months and stars turn as they will; let mountains and rivers change hands as they may—I hold fast to my own heart and cultivate myself. However good the world, I am still only myself; however wicked the age, I am still only myself. And should I shed this mortal frame, it would remain so. All of us who study the sword and the martial arts must guard our true heart, take the sword's two edges as a mirror, never be ashamed to ask and always seek the answer within ourselves, stay humble yet never cease striving, feel no dread in hardship, remain watchful even at feasts and revels, and show no fear before the powerful.
